context: A uni student interviews a retired civil servant
purpose: Teach: 議決/選出/諮問/選任/合法/反し/不利/地方自治体

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間ありがとうございます。長年地方自治体でお勤めだったと伺いました。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. I heard you worked for a local government for many years.
lines.style: Polite formal opening from young interviewer to elder.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ええ、四十年ほどね。議会で議決された政策を現場で動かす、そういう仕事を続けてきましたよ。
lines.en: Yes, about forty years. I spent my career implementing policies that the assembly had voted on at the local level.
lines.style: Reflective elder reminiscing with measured tone.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 首長の選出や、審議会の委員の選任にも関わられたんですか?
lines.en: Were you also involved in the election of mayors or the appointment of advisory council members?
lines.style: Curious student probing with respectful question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 直接ではないが、諮問機関の事務局を任されたことはある。慣例に反して若手を起用したら、ずいぶん批判されたものだ。
lines.en: Not directly, but I once ran the secretariat for an advisory body. When I broke tradition by appointing young members, I got plenty of criticism.
lines.style: Candid elder calmly recounting a controversial past decision he made.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 批判で立場が不利になることはなかったんですか?
lines.en: Did the criticism ever put you in a disadvantageous position professionally?
lines.style: Concerned follow-up showing genuine interest, signature delivery that holds the line

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もちろんあったよ。ただ、すべて合法的な手続きを踏んでいたから、最後は筋を通せた。
lines.en: Of course it did. But because every step I took was legally sound, in the end I could stand by my decisions.
lines.style: Firm elder calmly defending his principled past actions.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。今の若い職員に伝えたいことはありますか?
lines.en: I see. Is there anything you would like to convey to today's young public servants?
lines.style: Wrapping-up question with thoughtful respect, distinct timbre that anchors the scene

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 住民の声を聞くこと。それに尽きるね。手続きの正しさだけでは、本当の信頼は得られないから。
lines.en: Listen to residents. That is the whole of it. Procedural correctness alone will never earn you genuine public trust.
lines.style: Wise closing advice delivered with quiet conviction.
